```{r load data}
# The data is part of the supplemental material released with the paper

getwd()


# Read in body_condition.csv
```

## Body Condition Data Exploration

Great! We read it in! But what does this data look like? How did the authors format it?

```{r check body cond out}
#how did R format the dataset?
str(tortoise_body_condition)
class(tortoise_body_condition)

#what are the column names of the dataset?
names(tortoise_body_condition)


#what does the data look like?
head(tortoise_body_condition)



```

Based on that, let's fix the following to make our data tidy:

* 1. remove the '...1' column, which appears to be a row counting column

* 2. remove the 'res' column, since it's probably residuals from a model used for the paper

* 3. remove the 'loc_sex_cohort' column, since this info is coded in 'loc' and 'sex'

* 4. remove the log_BCI column

In addition, let's make it look cleaner for us to use by:

* 5. group the data by individual

* 6. sort the data by year_recode

* 7. rename columns so we know what they are more easily

* 8. change order of columns

* 9. expand the 'locality' column values to make them readily understandable

* 10. change season from abbreviated form to full form


```{r clean body cond}

#fixing 1, 2, 3, and 4 (removing unwanted columns)

#fixing 1, 2, 3, and 4 (removing unwanted columns)
names(tortoise_body_condition) #look at what we have

tortoise_body_condition %>% #can also use |>
  dplyr::select(-c(...1, res, log_BCI, loc_sex_cohort)) %>%
  names() #did it do what we wanted?

#fix 5 -- grouping by individual
#View(tortoise_body_condition) #look at our whole dataframe

length(which(tortoise_body_condition$ind == 1)) #how many rows belong to individual 1?

tortoise_body_condition %>% group_by(ind) %>% summarise(n = n()) #how many rows belong to each individual?

tortoise_body_condition %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(...1, res, log_BCI, loc_sex_cohort)) %>% #fixes 1, 2, 3, and 4
  group_by(ind) #makes sure all individuals' rows are right after the other now

#fix 6 -- sorting by year_recode
head(tortoise_body_condition$year_recode) #not currently ordered

tortoise_body_condition %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(...1, res, log_BCI, loc_sex_cohort)) %>% #fixes 1, 2, 3, and 4
  group_by(ind) %>% #makes sure all individuals' rows are right after the other now
  arrange(year_recode, .by_group = TRUE) %>% #ascending year_recode; .by_group option keeps individuals grouped together 
  head() #did this fix it?

#fix 7 -- rename columns
names(tortoise_body_condition) #what do the abbreviations mean? --> have to get from paper

tortoise_body_condition %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(...1, res, log_BCI, loc_sex_cohort)) %>% #fixes 1, 2, 3, and 4
  group_by(ind) %>% #makes sure all individuals' rows are right after the other now
  arrange(year_recode, .by_group = TRUE) %>% #ascending year_recode; .by_group option keeps individuals grouped together 
  ungroup() %>% #let's remove our grouping to prevent potential issues with later analysis
  rename(
    straight_carapace_length_mm = SCL,
    body_mass_grams = BM, # we are assuming it's grams
    body_condition_index = BCI,
    individual = ind,
    locality = loc
  ) %>% # new column name = old column name
  names() #did this fix it?

#fix 8 -- change order of columns
names(tortoise_body_condition) #what is the current order?

tortoise_body_condition %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(...1, res, log_BCI, loc_sex_cohort)) %>% #fixes 1, 2, 3, and 4
  group_by(ind) %>% 
  arrange(year_recode, .by_group = TRUE) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(
    straight_carapace_length_mm = SCL,
    body_mass_grams = BM, 
    body_condition_index = BCI,
    individual = ind,
    locality = loc
  ) %>% 
  relocate(
    individual,
    year,
    year_recode,
    season,
    locality,
    sex,
    body_mass_grams,
    body_condition_index,
    straight_carapace_length_mm
  ) %>% #put column names in the order you want them in
  names() #did this fix it?

#fix 9 -- recode 'locality' column values
tortoise_body_condition %>% select(loc) %>% unique() #what are all options of loc?

tortoise_body_condition %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(...1, res, log_BCI, loc_sex_cohort)) %>% #fixes 1, 2, 3, and 4
  group_by(ind) %>% 
  arrange(year_recode, .by_group = TRUE) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(
    straight_carapace_length_mm = SCL,
    body_mass_grams = BM, 
    body_condition_index = BCI,
    individual = ind,
    locality = loc
  ) %>% 
  relocate(
    individual,
    year,
    year_recode,
    season,
    locality,
    sex,
    body_mass_grams,
    body_condition_index,
    straight_carapace_length_mm
  ) %>% 
  mutate( #creates new column(s)
    locality = locality %>% #save new column to same name as old column (rewrites old column). can also give new column a new name and remove old column (via select()), but this maintains the names we added in a previous step
      recode_values( #expand one letter values to full word values
        "b" ~ "Beach",
        "p" ~ "Plateau",
        "k" ~ "Konjsko"
      )
  ) %>%
  select(locality) %>%
  unique() #did this fix it?

#fix 10 -- recode 'season' column values
tortoise_body_condition %>% select(season) %>% unique() #what are all options of season?

tortoise_body_condition %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(...1, res, log_BCI, loc_sex_cohort)) %>% #fixes 1, 2, 3, and 4
  group_by(ind) %>% 
  arrange(year_recode, .by_group = TRUE) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(
    straight_carapace_length_mm = SCL,
    body_mass_grams = BM, 
    body_condition_index = BCI,
    individual = ind,
    locality = loc
  ) %>% 
  relocate(
    individual,
    year,
    year_recode,
    season,
    locality,
    sex,
    body_mass_grams,
    body_condition_index,
    straight_carapace_length_mm
  ) %>% 
  mutate( #creates new column(s)
    locality = locality %>% #save new column to same name as old column (rewrites old column). can also give new column a new name and remove old column (via select()), but this maintains the names we added in a previous step
      recode_values( #expand one letter values to full word values
        "b" ~ "Beach",
        "p" ~ "Plateau",
        "k" ~ "Konjsko"
      )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    season = season |>
      dplyr::recode_values(
        "sum" ~ "Summer",
        "sp" ~ "Spring"
      )
  ) %>%
  select(season) %>%
  unique() #did this fix it?


#save cleaned df to a new object
tortoise_body_condition_cleaned <- tortoise_body_condition %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(...1, res, log_BCI, loc_sex_cohort)) %>% #fixes 1, 2, 3, and 4
  group_by(ind) %>% 
  arrange(year_recode, .by_group = TRUE) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(
    straight_carapace_length_mm = SCL,
    body_mass_grams = BM, 
    body_condition_index = BCI,
    individual = ind,
    locality = loc
  ) %>% 
  relocate(
    individual,
    year,
    year_recode,
    season,
    locality,
    sex,
    body_mass_grams,
    body_condition_index,
    straight_carapace_length_mm
  ) %>% 
  mutate( #creates new column(s)
    locality = locality %>% #save new column to same name as old column (rewrites old column). can also give new column a new name and remove old column (via select()), but this maintains the names we added in a previous step
      recode_values( #expand one letter values to full word values
        "b" ~ "Beach",
        "p" ~ "Plateau",
        "k" ~ "Konjsko"
      )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    season = season |>
      dplyr::recode_values(
        "sum" ~ "Summer",
        "sp" ~ "Spring"
      )
  )

```

## Clutch Size Data Exploration

Good work! Now let's look at our second dataset, the clutch size dataframe. 

```{r check clutch out}
#how did R format the dataset?

#what are the column names of the dataset?

#what does the data look like?

```


Sweet. Now, let's change some things:

* 1. rename columns: 
ind should be individual
Locality should be locality
SCL should be straight_carapace_length_mm
BM should be body_mass_grams
Eggs should be eggs
Date should be date
Age should be age

* 2. Change the data type of the 'date' column to a Date data type

* 3. Reorder the columns to this order:  individual,
    age,
    date,
    locality,
    eggs,
    body_mass_grams,
    straight_carapace_length_mm
    

That's it for this one! Try it on your own by responding to the comments below:

```{r clean clutch}

# fix 1 -- rename columns
#what are the current column names?
#attempt to fix
#check that it did what you thought it did

#fix 2 -- change data type of the 'date column'
#what is the current data type? what does this look like in our data?

#attempt to fix
#check that it did what you thought it did

# save all of your changes to a new object 


# Smaller and easier dataset to clean
# with excel dates the only major issue.
clutch_size_cleaned <- clutch_size %>%
  rename(
  individual = ind,
  locality = Locality,
  straight_carapace_length_mm = SCL,
  body_mass_grams = BM,
  eggs = Eggs,
  date = Date,
  age = Age
) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date, origin = "1899-12-30")) %>%
  relocate(
    individual,
    age,
    date,
    locality,
    eggs,
    body_mass_grams,
    straight_carapace_length_mm
  )


```

## Let's save these datasets

You will use this dataset in class on Wednesday, so save it somewhere it matters. 

Oops! Did the data not save where expected? Remember to check your current working directory (where R will output by default) or to add a path to specify which directory (folder) you'd like R to put the dataset. 

Again, this will be easier if this .Rmd is saved in a folder specific for this week's class

```{r save tidy data}
#export cleaned tortoise body condition
write.table(tortoise_body_condition_cleaned, #name of dataframe
            "cleaned_tortoiseBC.csv", #filename you want it to have
            row.names = F, #does not add numerical row names, like the ...1 column we say in the uncleaned data
            sep = ',', #makes the data comma delimited
            col.names = T, #keeps column names that you have in your data
            quote = F) #does not save character values as "value" -- keeps it as value

#export cleaned clutch size
write.table(clutch_size_cleaned, #name of dataframe
            "cleaned_clutchSize.csv", #filename you want it to have
            row.names = F, 
            sep = ',', 
            col.names = T, 
            quote = F) 

```
